To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) audit fees in Italy are affected by the size of the audited entity, its complexity and audit risk; (2) the large auditor premium is only present for KPMG; and (3) the large auditor fee premium is not related to auditor size, but to the specific characteristics of the audit firm.
audit fees in the large audit market in Italy are affected by the size and complexity of the auditee, the complexity of the audit, and the auditor size.
the fee model developed for the Italian market shows that the size, complexity of auditees, and audit risk are the most relevant variables that explain audit fees.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determinants of the audit fee paid in the Italian market.
the determinants of the audit fees paid by the largest Italian companies.
the audit fee model and the large auditor premium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
audit fee determinants are the same in Italy and in other countries, but the large auditor premium is only for one firm.
the Italian market is not different from other European markets in terms of fee determinants.
the Big Six auditors as a whole did not accrue any premium, while the premium accrued by KPMG could be justified by its higher quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the Italian market, the audit fees are determined by the size of auditee and by audit risk.
the Big Six in Italy did not accrue an additional fee for their audit services.
the audit market in Italy has not reached a competitive equilibrium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Italian Antitrust decision should be reconsidered.
the audit fees paid by Italian clients are in line with those of other European countries, and the large audit firms are not overcharging.
the audit market in Italy is not different from other countries in terms of audit fees.
